newsitem.title: INDIA: Polls in India's Punjab put off by a day to Feb 7.
newsitem.headline: Polls in India's Punjab put off by a day to Feb 7.

text.p: India's Election Commission has postponed assembly elections in the northern state of Punjab by one day to February 7, the Press Trust of India (PTI) said on Monday.
A by-election to the Ropar parliamentary seat in Punjab has also been postponed by a day, to February 7, PTI said.

By-elections to three seats of the Lok Sabha, the lower house of the federal parliament, and 15 assembly seats in states other than Punjab will now be held on February 8 instead of February 6 as scheduled, the news agency said.

The delay became necessary following the declaration of a national holiday on January 23 to mark the birth centenary of Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose, who helped lead the Indian struggle for independence from Britain, PTI said.
It said polling schedules had been changed only in those constitutencies whose original election schedules were affected by the holiday.
The counting of votes will begin on February 9 in Punjab and February 11 in the other elections, PTI said.
